parts:
:::writing{variant="email" id="48271" subject="Re: Your Formal Notice"}
Aanchal,

First of all... if an email from you ever starts with **"This is my formal resignation..."** again, I am going to die. 😂 I literally almost threw up in my mouth when I read the first few lines. Next time, maybe lead with, "Don't panic..." because you absolutely got me.

Now that I've recovered...

I honestly don't even know where to begin.

I am so incredibly proud of you. Watching your growth over the past several months has been one of the greatest joys of building this company. You've challenged yourself, stepped outside your comfort zone, and continually looked for ways to make yourself and this business better. That mindset is rare.

The truth is, I could not have built The Luxora Collective without you. You have been my rock through so many moving pieces, and your loyalty, commitment, organization, and willingness to jump into anything we've needed have made you an invaluable part of this company. I hope you know how deeply appreciated you are.

Reading your email honestly made me smile.

You're absolutely right. We are in startup mode, wearing every hat imaginable, and if we're going to build the company we all envision, we have to create systems that can operate beyond us. Building an operational backbone, creating SOPs, documenting responsibilities, developing hiring frameworks, and making our company truly scalable is exactly where we need to go.

I also love that you're not coming into this thinking you have every answer. You're coming with humility, curiosity, drive, and a willingness to learn, and those qualities matter far more than pretending to know everything. Your conversation with Jhana and the initiative you've taken only reinforces what we've already seen in you.

What stood out to me the most was that you're not asking to do less. You're asking to do more. You're willing to continue carrying your EA responsibilities while proving yourself in this next season, and that says everything about your character.

Eric and I have always wanted people on this team who think like owners, who look ahead instead of waiting to be told what to do, and who genuinely care about building something bigger than themselves. This email embodies exactly that.

So yes, we're excited.

We're excited to keep talking through this with you, to shape what this role looks like together, and to watch you grow into an operational leader within TLC. I truly believe this is the beginning of another chapter in your journey, and I cannot wait to see what you're capable of.

Thank you for believing in our vision. Thank you for believing in me. And thank you for helping build something that I genuinely believe is going to change this industry.

Now... please never scare me like that again. 😂

We love you, we're proud of you, and we're so excited for what's ahead.

❤️
Bethany (and Eric)
:::

Respond to her in the most loving way. Letting her know that I am so proud of her and it has been an honor to watch her grow along this journey. I couldn't have created this business without her. She's been a rock and an invaluable piece of the Luxora Collective. And then mention if she ever starts a message. This is my formal resignation... I will die. I literally almost threw up in my mouth. And then say some funny line about it. Let her know each points of her at email. Respond to it with agreement and excitement for the future. We're looking forward to connecting more on this and seeing her girl in the operational position. 

This is her email
Hi Bethany and Eric,

I wanted to put this in writing, because I feel you both deserve that.

This is my formal notice.

Working alongside you both has been one of the most formative experiences of my career. Bethany, watching you operate, the way you show up for clients, the way you have built something from nothing, has genuinely changed how I see what is possible. You inspire me everyday. Eric, your steadiness, your vision, and the way you have welcomed me into this has meant more than I have ever said out loud. You both took a chance on me and gave me room to grow into myself professionally, and I will carry that with me regardless of where life takes me.

However, I see more for myself.

Not more elsewhere.

More here.

This is not a resignation. This is a pitch.

Now that we are actively hiring closers, the timing feels right to bring something forward that I have been sitting with for a while. I would like to step into an operational leadership role within TLC.

Here is my honest thinking. We are in startup mode. We are all wearing many hats, and that is exactly right for where we are. But if we are serious about becoming Limitless-adjacent and eventually acquirable, we need to be operationally structured. Right now, none of our roles are truly duplicatable. If any one of us had to step away tomorrow, there is no clean playbook, no defined scope, no way to bring someone in and replace that person seamlessly. Gil cannot acquire what he cannot replace, and right now, he cannot replace any of us. That is the gap I want to help close.

What I am proposing is that I begin building the operational backbone of the agency: role-specific responsibilities, SOPs, hiring and performance frameworks, and the kind of structure a future acquirer could actually step into and scale. I am not asking to make the calls on people. I want to be the one observing, flagging, and bringing recommendations to you both so that you can make those executive decisions with the full picture.

I will be honest. I do not have all the answers and I am not coming in claiming to know how to run an agency. But I have the drive, I have the resource of Limitless, and I had a call with Jhana yesterday where she affirmed my approach entirely. That conversation gave me the confidence to bring this to you properly, in writing, the way you deserve.

I can talk at length about what I want to do. But more than anything, I just want to show you.

As for my EA responsibilities, they are not going anywhere. Not until we are in a place to bring on another EA and make that transition properly. I am not asking to step back from anything. I am asking to step into something more. And to be clear, this is not about compensation. Not right now. All I am asking for is a yes and the room to prove that this was the right call. If I do that, I trust that everything else will follow in time.

Thank you for building something worth showing up for. 

Best,
Aanchal
